# Feature: Workflow Replay

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-010
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan.md`

`yantra run <workflow-name>` turns a saved workflow YAML into a one-command, deterministic, checkpointed, auditable execution — and `yantra resume <run-id>` picks up where a failed or paused run left off. This is the **second user-visible slice** of the MVP: combined with FEAT-008 (recorder) and FEAT-009 (annotate + YAML emit), the user has a complete **record → annotate → replay** loop. Concretely:

```
$ yantra run bank-statement --month=2026-04
   loading workflow… ok
   resolved params: { month: "2026-04" }
   acquiring profile: profiles/bank-statement (cookies=auto)
   step 1/9  navigate https://mybank.example/login            ✓
   step 2/9  fill   "Username field"  ••••• (secret:bank.username)  ✓
   …
   ✓ run complete — report: runs/01J7K…-bank-statement/report.md
```

This feature owns the **`yantra run` orchestrator** — the glue between every preceding feature:

- It calls the **WorkflowStore** (FEAT-009) to load and parse the YAML.
- It re-runs **schema + semantic validation** (FEAT-002) against the loaded `Workflow`.
- It translates the persisted `Workflow` into the in-memory `Plan` the executor consumes (Workflow is essentially a hand-authored/recorded Plan with named locators — same conceptual model, two serialization layers).
- It resolves CLI/file params against the workflow's declared params block.
- It instantiates the **ExecutionContext** with the workflow's profile (FEAT-003), bound secret resolver (FEAT-006), and configured budgets.
- It drives the **Executor** (FEAT-005), which walks candidate chains (FEAT-004), checkpoints per step, emits events, and enforces ethics/scopes.
- On termination — success, failure, or human-handoff abort — it writes `outputs.json` and renders `report.md`.
- `yantra resume <run-id>` rehydrates state from the run directory + the executor's checkpoint store and continues from the last-saved step.

**Why this matters as one feature:** every responsibility above is tightly coupled to one thing — *the lifecycle of a single `Run`*. Splitting the orchestrator from the report renderer or from the resume entry point would force three features to share a half-baked notion of run state. Combined, this feature has one job: take a workflow name and produce a complete, audited run directory.

This feature unblocks:
- **FEAT-012 (CLI Polish)** — `yantra run` and `yantra resume` are top-level commands in the final command surface; the report renderer is reused by `yantra audit <run-id>` and `yantra report <run-id>`.
- The user-visible **record-then-replay round-trip** dogfooding milestone called out in plan §2 ("after FEAT-010 a working `record`+`run`").

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> Filesystem-only — no database in MVP. The "data model" here is on-disk artifacts plus the in-memory types that consume them. A forward-looking SQLite sketch is included for the Phase 2 daemon.

### Workflow → Plan Translation (conceptual)

This feature owns the mapping between the **persisted** `Workflow` (YAML) and the **in-memory** `Plan` the executor consumes. The two are mostly isomorphic by design — Workflow is a Plan with one extra indirection (named locators).

| Workflow concept (FEAT-009 / FEAT-002) | Plan concept (FEAT-002, executed by FEAT-005) |
|---|---|
| `workflow.name`, `workflow.version` | recorded in `manifest.json`; not directly part of `Plan` |
| `workflow.params: { month: {type, example, ...} }` (declaration) | resolved at orchestrator boundary into a `Record<string, unknown>` available to step substitution; `ParamRef` in steps refers to keys here |
| `workflow.secrets: [ "bank.username" ]` (declaration) | unchanged — `SecretRef.key` in steps refers to these keys; resolved at execution boundary by FEAT-006 |
| `workflow.cookies: auto \| none` | maps to `ProfileSpec` for FEAT-003 (`auto` → `{kind:"workflow", workflowName}`; `none` → `{kind:"ephemeral"}`) |
| `workflow.steps[i]` (one of navigate / click / fill / extract / wait_for / assert / branch / loop / call_workflow / llm_summarize) | `Plan.steps[i]` — same discriminated union from `packages/protocol`. Translator assigns `step.id` deterministically (`s1`..`sN`) if not present. |
| `workflow.steps[i].scope?: "public" \| "read-only-data" \| "authenticated"` | preserved 1:1 on `Plan.steps[i].scope` |
| Step locator references (string key into `_locators`, e.g. `"Username field"`) | `LocatorChain` of kind `{ kind: "workflow", name: "Username field" }` — preserves the indirection; the engine (FEAT-004) walks the chain by name at execution time |
| `workflow._locators: { "<name>": [candidate, …] }` | carried alongside the Plan as `Plan.locatorTable` (or attached to the `ExecutionContext` — see implementation note below) |
| `workflow.outputs: [{ summary: "{{ capture:summary }}" }]` | `Plan.outputs` — declared output bindings; orchestrator evaluates these JSONata expressions at run end against accumulated captures |

**Implementation note:** the Plan emitted by the agent in FEAT-011 doesn't carry a locator table (the agent gets locator-by-name resolution for free via the workflow). For replay, we attach the workflow's `_locators` block to the `ExecutionContext`, not to the `Plan` itself — keeping the `Plan` shape identical to what the agent produces means FEAT-005 has *one* execution path, not two. The translator's output is `{ plan: Plan, locatorTable: LocatorTable }` and both flow into the context.

### On-Disk Artifacts

Per-run directory at `~/.local/share/yantra/runs/<run-id>/`. Run-id format: `<iso8601-compact>-<workflow-name>-<short-uuid>` (e.g. `20260511T091234Z-bank-statement-a7b3` — ISO-timestamp-prefixed for natural sort; workflow name aids glob; short UUID dedupes within the same second). This feature **owns** the contents of `manifest.json`, `outputs.json`, `report.md`, and writes `events.jsonl` via the executor's emitter (FEAT-005). It does **not** own `plan.json`, `agent.jsonl`, `secrets.jsonl`, or `checkpoints/` — those are written by FEAT-002/006/005 respectively; this feature *reads* them when rendering the report.

| Artifact | Path | Lifecycle | Permissions | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Run root** | `~/.local/share/yantra/runs/<run-id>/` | Created at `RunOrchestrator.run()` start; never deleted by Yantra (user-owned). | `0700` (Unix); inherit-from-parent on Windows. | `RunStore` (this feature) |
| **`manifest.json`** | `<run-root>/manifest.json` | Written once, atomically, at run start. Re-written once at run end with `ended_at`, `status`, `duration_ms`, `failure_class?`. | `0600`. | `manifest-writer.ts` (this feature) |
| **`plan.json`** | `<run-root>/plan.json` | Written once at run start, immediately after Workflow→Plan translation. Read by resume. | `0600`. | written by orchestrator via FEAT-002 schemas; *consumed* by report renderer. |
| **`events.jsonl`** | `<run-root>/events.jsonl` | Append-only stream produced by FEAT-005's event bus; *consumed* by report renderer. | `0600`. | FEAT-005. |
| **`agent.jsonl`** | `<run-root>/agent.jsonl` | Append-only; empty for replay runs (no LLM calls) unless the Plan contains an `llm_summarize` step. | `0600`. | FEAT-006. |
| **`secrets.jsonl`** | `<run-root>/secrets.jsonl` | Append-only key-lookup log (no values). | `0600`. | FEAT-006. |
| **`checkpoints/`** | `<run-root>/checkpoints/` | One `step-<id>.json` per successful step. | `0600`. | FEAT-005. |
| **`outputs.json`** | `<run-root>/outputs.json` | Written once at run end (success or failure-with-partial-captures). Workflow's declared outputs evaluated through JSONata against captures; retention metadata included. | `0600`. | `manifest-writer.ts` (this feature). |
| **`report.md`** | `<run-root>/report.md` | Written once at run end (always — success, failure, or abort). | `0600`. | `report-renderer.ts` (this feature). |
| **Run-dir lockfile** | `<run-root>/.lock` | Created at run start with PID; removed on clean exit. Prevents accidental concurrent resume of the same run. | `0600`. | `RunStore`. |

**Atomic-write convention** (manifest.json, outputs.json, report.md): write to `<file>.tmp`, fsync, rename — same pattern as FEAT-009's workflow YAML writes. Pino's append-only writes to `events.jsonl` etc. are not atomic per-line but never overwrite.

### In-Memory Entities

```ts
// packages/core/src/workflow/replay/types.ts (this feature)

/** Top-level request constructed by apps/cli from argv. Zod-validated. */
interface RunRequest {
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;     // already merged from --params + --params-file
  readonly budgets: RunBudgets;
  readonly json: boolean;                                  // --json flag — emit structured stdout
  readonly debug: boolean;                                 // --debug — stream events to stdout too
}

interface RunBudgets {
  readonly stepRetries: number;          // override of workflow / executor default
  readonly wallClockMs: number;          // hard ceiling for the run
  readonly humanWaitMs: number;          // ceiling for human-handoff interactive waits
}

/** Live in-memory entity for one execution. Created by RunOrchestrator. */
interface Run {
  readonly runId: string;                                  // <iso>-<wf>-<short-uuid>
  readonly taskId: string;                                 // ulid; distinct so resume runs can chain task_ids
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly workflowVersion: number;
  readonly type: "run";                                    // future: "resume"
  readonly plan: Plan;                                     // from protocol; produced by translator
  readonly ctx: ExecutionContext;                          // from FEAT-005
  status: "queued" | "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "aborted" | "paused";
  readonly startedAt: string;                              // ISO-8601
  endedAt: string | null;
  failureClass: FailureClass | null;                       // from FEAT-005's taxonomy
  lastCheckpointStepId: string | null;                     // updated as checkpoints flush
}

/** Returned by RunOrchestrator.run() — the CLI maps these to exit codes. */
type RunOutcome =
  | { kind: "success";  runId: string; outputs: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> }
  | { kind: "failure";  runId: string; failureClass: FailureClass; reportPath: string }
  | { kind: "aborted";  runId: string; reason: "user-handoff" | "scope-violation" | "ethics-refused"; reportPath: string };

/** What `yantra resume` consumes to continue. Plan §4: checkpoint is a LOGICAL POINTER, not a browser-state snapshot. */
interface ResumePoint {
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly lastCheckpointStepId: string;
  readonly nextStepIndex: number;                          // index into Plan.steps to resume *from*
  readonly captures: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;    // captures so far, rehydrated from checkpoint contents
  readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;      // original run's params (re-resolve secrets at exec boundary)
  readonly cookieProfilePath: string | null;               // workflow profile reuse
  readonly originalFailureClass: FailureClass | null;      // used to gate "should you resume this?"
  readonly originalStartedAt: string;                      // for the >24h stale-resume confirmation prompt
}

/** Output of the Workflow → Plan translator. */
interface TranslatedWorkflow {
  readonly plan: Plan;                                     // from protocol
  readonly locatorTable: LocatorTable;                     // map of name → LocatorChain[], from FEAT-002/009
  readonly profileSpec: ProfileSpec;                       // derived from workflow.cookies
  readonly outputBindings: readonly OutputBinding[];       // evaluated at run end
  readonly declaredSecretKeys: readonly string[];          // pre-flight check that each secret exists in keychain
}

interface OutputBinding {
  readonly name: string;                                   // e.g. "summary"
  readonly expression: string;                             // raw JSONata, evaluated against captures + final ctx
  readonly retention: "transient" | "persisted";           // honored by manifest writer; "transient" omitted from outputs.json
}

/** What gets serialized to manifest.json. Secrets and PII never appear. */
interface RunManifest {
  readonly schemaVersion: "0.1";
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly taskId: string;
  readonly type: "run" | "resume";
  readonly parentRunId: string | null;                     // populated for resume runs
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly workflowVersion: number;
  readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;      // resolved params with SecretRef values REDACTED to `{ kind:"secret", key }`
  readonly startedAt: string;
  endedAt: string | null;
  status: Run["status"];
  durationMs: number | null;
  failureClass: FailureClass | null;
  readonly scopeSummary: ScopeSummary;                     // counts of steps per scope
  readonly llmProvider: "anthropic" | "ollama" | "none";   // from config at run start
  readonly cookieMode: "auto" | "none";
  readonly profilePath: string | null;                     // null if ephemeral
  // Chrome version drift signal — plan §6:
  readonly recordedWith: { chromeMajor: number; yantraVersion: string } | null;  // from Workflow.recorded_with
  readonly chromeAtRun: { major: number; full: string };   // from FEAT-003 Browser.getVersion at run start
  readonly chromeDriftWarning: string | null;              // populated when |chromeAtRun.major - recordedWith.chromeMajor| > 2
  readonly unrecordedFrameOrigins: readonly string[];      // copied from Workflow._unrecorded_frames; replay uses for diagnostics
}

interface ScopeSummary {
  readonly publicCount: number;
  readonly readOnlyDataCount: number;
  readonly authenticatedCount: number;
}

/** What gets serialized to outputs.json. */
interface RunOutputs {
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly emittedAt: string;
  readonly outputs: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;     // retention=persisted only
  readonly retentionPolicy: "default" | "extended";        // pulled from workflow; defaults to "default"
}

/** Structured report data used by ReportRenderer. */
interface RunReport {
  readonly run: Run;
  readonly manifest: RunManifest;
  readonly events: readonly TaskEvent[];                   // from events.jsonl
  readonly checkpoints: readonly CheckpointSummary[];      // names + step ids; not full payloads
  readonly outputs: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  readonly failure: FailureDetail | null;
}

interface FailureDetail {
  readonly failureClass: FailureClass;
  readonly lastAttemptedStepId: string;
  readonly candidatesTried: readonly { kind: string; matched: boolean }[];
  readonly sanitizerSummary: string;                       // e.g. "12 form fields stripped"
  readonly scopeViolation: { scope: string; verb: string; stepId: string } | null;
}
```

### Repository-Style Interfaces

```ts
/** Filesystem-based repository for runs. Mockable in tests; swaps to SQLite in Phase 2. */
interface RunStore {
  /** Create the run dir + .lock, return the canonical runId. */
  createRun(request: RunRequest): Promise<{ runId: string; runDir: string }>;

  /** List recent runs sorted by startedAt desc; filter by workflow / status. */
  listRuns(opts?: { workflowName?: string; status?: Run["status"]; limit?: number }): Promise<readonly RunSummary[]>;

  /** Load a run dir's manifest + minimal index. Returns null if not found. */
  getRun(runId: string): Promise<Run | null>;

  /** Atomic status update on manifest.json. */
  updateRunStatus(runId: string, patch: { status: Run["status"]; endedAt?: string; failureClass?: FailureClass; lastCheckpointStepId?: string }): Promise<void>;

  /** Remove the .lock file. Idempotent. */
  releaseLock(runId: string): Promise<void>;
}

interface RunSummary {
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly workflowVersion: number;
  readonly status: Run["status"];
  readonly startedAt: string;
  readonly endedAt: string | null;
  readonly durationMs: number | null;
  readonly failureClass: FailureClass | null;
}

/** Renders a RunReport into a markdown string. Pure function — no side effects. */
interface ReportRenderer {
  renderRunReport(report: RunReport): string;
  renderJsonSummary(report: RunReport): RunJsonSummary;   // --json flag path
}

interface RunJsonSummary {
  readonly runId: string;
  readonly workflowName: string;
  readonly status: Run["status"];
  readonly durationMs: number | null;
  readonly stepsCompleted: number;
  readonly stepsTotal: number;
  readonly outputs: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  readonly failure: FailureDetail | null;
  readonly reportPath: string;
}
```

### Forward-Looking DB Schema Sketch (Phase 2 daemon — not built here)

When the Phase 2 daemon arrives, runs metadata moves to SQLite (the run-dir artifacts stay on disk; the DB indexes them). Capturing the sketch now so the filesystem format stays compatible:

```sql
-- Phase 2 only. NOT created by this feature.
CREATE TABLE runs (
  run_id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  task_id             TEXT NOT NULL,
  parent_run_id       TEXT REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  type                TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('run','resume')),
  workflow_name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  workflow_version    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  status              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('queued','running','completed','failed','aborted','paused')),
  started_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
  ended_at            TEXT,
  duration_ms         INTEGER,
  failure_class       TEXT,
  llm_provider        TEXT,
  cookie_mode         TEXT NOT NULL,
  run_dir             TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE
);
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_workflow_started ON runs (workflow_name, started_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_status ON runs (status);

CREATE TABLE run_outputs (
  run_id              TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  output_name         TEXT NOT NULL,
  output_value_json   TEXT NOT NULL,    -- JSON-encoded value; secrets never appear
  retention           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (retention IN ('transient','persisted')),
  emitted_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, output_name)
);
```

### Relationships

- One `Workflow` (owned by FEAT-009) → 1:N `Run`s.
- One `Run` → 1:1 `RunManifest`, 1:1 `RunOutputs`, 1:1 `report.md`, 1:N `TaskEvent`s, 1:N checkpoints.
- One `Run` → 0:1 `parentRunId` (for `yantra resume` continuations). A resume creates a *new* run row with a new `runId` and a `parentRunId` pointer; the original run's manifest is *not* mutated. This keeps run history append-only.
- One `Run` ↔ 1:1 profile dir when `cookieMode === "auto"` (the same dir is shared across all runs of the workflow — owned by FEAT-003's `ProfileStore`).

### Indexes & Constraints (filesystem-level)

- **Unique constraint**: `runId` is unique by construction (ISO timestamp + short UUID).
- **Lock constraint**: `<run-root>/.lock` prevents accidental concurrent resume of the same run dir; check is best-effort (PID liveness on Unix; on Windows we accept staleness — orchestrator validates `Run.status` is in `{failed, paused}` before resume regardless).
- **Append-only constraint**: `events.jsonl`, `agent.jsonl`, `secrets.jsonl` are never rewritten — only appended. The resume orchestrator appends a fresh `task_resumed` event rather than mutating prior events.
- **Permission constraint**: every file in `<run-root>` is `0600` Unix; the dir is `0700`. Enforced at write time. `yantra doctor` (FEAT-003) flags violations.

## 3. Files

Source files (all new):

- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/types.ts` — All type definitions for this feature: `RunRequest`, `RunBudgets`, `Run`, `RunOutcome`, `ResumePoint`, `TranslatedWorkflow`, `OutputBinding`, `RunManifest`, `ScopeSummary`, `RunOutputs`, `RunReport`, `FailureDetail`, `RunSummary`, `RunJsonSummary`, `CheckpointSummary`. Re-exports `FailureClass` and `TaskEvent` from `packages/protocol` (type-only). Error classes barrel-exported from `errors.ts`.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/errors.ts` — Custom error classes: `WorkflowNotFoundError`, `ParamsValidationError`, `MissingRequiredParamError`, `WorkflowTranslationError`, `RunNotResumableError`, `RunDirMissingError`, `RunDirLockedError`, `OutputEvaluationError`. Each extends `Error` and carries structured context.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/params-resolver.ts` — `resolveParams(input: { cli: ParamArg[]; file?: string; workflowParams: WorkflowParamsSpec }): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`. Reads `--params-file` YAML (using `yaml` package — same as FEAT-009), merges `--params key=val` on top (CLI wins), coerces each value to the type declared in `workflow.params` (string / number / boolean / date), validates required-ness, surfaces typed errors. Defense-in-depth: refuses values that look like secrets (sk-, ghp_, AKIA, eyJ…) — params are not secrets.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/workflow-to-plan.ts` — `translate(workflow: Workflow, params: Record<string, unknown>): TranslatedWorkflow`. Pure function. Walks `workflow.steps`, assigns deterministic step ids, preserves scopes, builds the `LocatorChain` references (`{ kind: "workflow", name }`), extracts `outputBindings` from `workflow.outputs`, computes `profileSpec` from `workflow.cookies`, collects `declaredSecretKeys`. Re-runs the FEAT-002 semantic validator on the produced Plan as belt-and-suspenders.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/run-store.ts` — `LocalRunStore implements RunStore`. Filesystem repo: `createRun` builds the run dir (`paths.dataDir()/runs/<runId>/`) with `0700` perms + `.lock` file; `listRuns` does a `readdir` + parses each `manifest.json`; `getRun` reads one manifest; `updateRunStatus` atomically rewrites manifest.json; `releaseLock` removes `.lock`. Path helpers reuse FEAT-003's `paths.ts`.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/manifest-writer.ts` — `writeManifest(runDir, manifest)`, `updateManifest(runDir, patch)`, `writeOutputs(runDir, outputs)`. Atomic-write convention (tmp + rename). Includes `redactParamsForManifest(params, declaredSecretKeys)` helper that walks the params record and replaces any value matching a declared secret with `{ kind: "secret", key }`.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/output-evaluator.ts` — `evaluateOutputs(bindings: OutputBinding[], context: { captures, params, finalCtx }): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`. JSONata evaluation under FEAT-005's expression-engine sandbox (200 ms timeout, 100 KB result cap, no custom functions). Filters by `retention` for `outputs.json`. Surfaces evaluation failures as `OutputEvaluationError` with the offending binding name; the run does NOT fail because of an output-eval error — it logs `warn` and emits a `report.md` warning section (the data was extracted; user can inspect captures).
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/report-renderer.ts` — `MarkdownReportRenderer implements ReportRenderer`. Sections per spec: Summary, Steps, Outputs, Failure Detail (if applicable), Audit. Pure string templating; no I/O. The Playwright-call-log shape from brainstorm §7.6 is used for per-step rendering. Also exports `renderJsonSummary(report)` for `--json`.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/cookies-mode.ts` — Tiny helper: `cookieModeToProfileSpec(mode: "auto"|"none", workflowName: string): ProfileSpec`. Single source of truth for the mapping. Exported so FEAT-008 (recorder) can reuse it.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/preflight.ts` — `preflightSecrets(declaredKeys, secretStore): Promise<PreflightResult>`. Calls `SecretStore.has(key)` for each declared key (FEAT-006); fails fast with `SecretNotFoundError` listing missing keys, before any browser launch. Cheap and high-signal.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/run-orchestrator.ts` — `RunOrchestrator` class. Constructor takes `{ workflowStore, runStore, browserProvider, secretStore, executor, sanitizer, ethicsGate, llmClient, logger, clock }` — pure DI, no module singletons. Methods: `run(request: RunRequest): Promise<RunOutcome>` and `resume(runId: string, opts: { json: boolean }): Promise<RunOutcome>` (resume delegates to `resume.ts` for the rehydration step; orchestration is shared).
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/resume.ts` — `loadResumePoint(runStore, runDir): Promise<ResumePoint>`. Reads `manifest.json`, validates status, scans `checkpoints/` for the highest-numbered step file, rehydrates captures. Exports `ResumeGuardError` and a confirm-required predicate `requiresUserConsent(originalFailureClass)` — true for `scope-violation` and `ethics-refused`.
- `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/index.ts` — Barrel export.

Test files (mirrored under `packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/`):

- `packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/params-resolver.spec.ts` — All coercion paths, --params-file precedence, missing-required errors, secret-shape rejection.

- `packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/preflight.spec.ts` — All declared keys present → ok; one missing → typed error with all missing keys listed (not just the first).
- `packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/run-orchestrator.spec.ts` — Orchestrator with fully mocked dependencies. Success path. Failure path (executor throws `LocatorNotFoundError` → report written → outcome `failure` → exit 2). Scope-violation path (planValidationError before browser instantiation → report written → outcome `aborted`/scope-violation → exit 2). Human-handoff path (executor emits `HumanHandoffRequested` with user choice "abort+checkpoint" → outcome `aborted`/user-handoff → exit 4).
- `packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/resume.spec.ts` — Resume of a paused run continues at the right step index; resume of a `completed` run errors with `RunNotResumableError`; resume of a `scope-violation` failure requires consent; checkpoint rehydration loads captures correctly.
- `packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/run-orchestrator.property.spec.ts` — `fast-check` property: random valid workflows + random valid params → orchestrator always returns a `RunOutcome` (never throws an uncaught error); a `report.md` is always written on completion or failure. Property echoes memory.md's "every aborted run produces report.md" guarantee.
- `e2e/record-replay/bank-statement-fixture.spec.ts` — Real end-to-end: record against a fixture HTTP server (FEAT-008) → YAML emit (FEAT-009) → replay (this feature) → assert `outputs.json` matches expected JSON, exit code 0, `report.md` non-empty. Tagged `@no-llm`; gated on `YANTRA_E2E_BROWSER=1`. **This is the dogfooding acceptance gate for the recorder/replay round-trip suite (memory.md §Testing).**

Configuration touches:

- `packages/core/package.json` — depends on `yaml` (already pulled by FEAT-009), `jsonata` (already pulled by FEAT-005), `zod` (workspace). No new deps unique to this feature.
- `apps/cli/src/commands/run.ts` (small wiring file — owned by FEAT-012, but stubbed here for the e2e test) — parses argv into `RunRequest`, calls `RunOrchestrator.run`, maps `RunOutcome` to exit code, renders stdout (markdown summary or `--json`).
- `apps/cli/src/commands/resume.ts` — parses `<run-id>`, calls `RunOrchestrator.resume`, same exit-code/stdout mapping.

## 4. Dependencies

**Internal (other Yantra features):**

- **FEAT-001 (Monorepo Scaffold & CI)** — required. Provides `packages/core/`, TS strict, Vitest, fast-check, the CI matrix that runs the e2e suite.
- **FEAT-002 (Yantra Protocol v0)** — required. The orchestrator consumes the `Workflow`, `Plan`, `Step`, `TaskEvent`, `LocatorChain`, `ValueRef`, `SecretRef` schemas. The translator re-runs the **semantic validator** from FEAT-002 against the produced Plan as belt-and-suspenders even though FEAT-009 already validates on save (defense-in-depth: a workflow edited by hand between save and run still gets caught here).
- **FEAT-003 (Chrome Launcher & BrowserProvider)** — required. The orchestrator instantiates a `BrowserSession` via `BrowserProvider.launch()` with the `ProfileSpec` derived from `workflow.cookies`. Per-workflow profile for `cookies: auto`; ephemeral for `cookies: none`.
- **FEAT-004 (Locator Engine & Auto-Wait)** — required (transitively, via FEAT-005). The Plan's `{ kind: "workflow", name }` locators are resolved by the engine against the `LocatorTable` attached to the `ExecutionContext`.
- **FEAT-005 (Plan Executor & Step Verbs)** — required. The orchestrator hands the `Plan` + `ExecutionContext` to `Executor.run()` and consumes the resulting `TaskEvent` stream. Checkpointing, retries, ethics gate, event emission, and step verbs are all FEAT-005's responsibility — this feature does not duplicate them.
- **FEAT-006 (Security Envelope)** — required. `SecretStore.has(key)` for preflight; `SecretStore.get(key)` is called by the executor (FEAT-005) at the execution boundary, not by this orchestrator directly. The `ScopeEnforcer` runs as part of FEAT-005's executor — this orchestrator just rolls up the scope summary into the manifest. The sanitizer (FEAT-006) is the only path to the LLM client for `llm_summarize` steps.
- **FEAT-009 (Annotate UI & Workflow YAML)** — required. The orchestrator calls `WorkflowStore.load(name)` to get a parsed, schema-validated `Workflow`. `yantra lint` validation is the same code path that runs here at load time.
- **FEAT-011 (Agent Integration)** — **not required.** Replay is deterministic by design (`@no-llm`). The only LLM touch point is an optional `llm_summarize` step inside a replay; if present and `LLM_PROVIDER=none`, FEAT-005 surfaces `LLMUnavailableError` which this orchestrator catches and renders into a clear "this workflow needs an LLM provider" report.

**External (npm):**

- `yaml` (already in workspace via FEAT-009) — parses `--params-file`.
- `jsonata` (already in workspace via FEAT-005) — output binding evaluation (same sandbox config).
- `zod` (workspace) — `RunRequest` and `RunManifest` schemas.
- `ulid` or `uuid` (already in workspace) — `taskId` generation; short-UUID suffix for `runId`.
- `vitest` (dev) — unit + integration runner.
- `fast-check` (dev) — property test on orchestrator robustness.

**Notes:**

- No `commander`-version-specific behavior here — argv parsing happens in FEAT-012's `apps/cli`. This feature's API surface is in-process; the CLI thin-shells it.
- No direct `keytar` import — all keychain access goes through FEAT-006's `SecretStore`.
- No direct `pi-agent-core` import — replay does not call the LLM client directly; FEAT-005's executor does that for `llm_summarize` via the `packages/agent` adapter.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

> Vertical slices. Tasks are ordered so a coding agent can start at TASK-001 and have something runnable (the orchestrator running against a fixture) by TASK-003. Later tasks layer on resume, cookie modes, structured outputs, and the e2e acceptance gate.

### TASK-001: ParamsResolver — CLI + file + defaults + type coercion

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `params-resolver.ts`.
  - Export `resolveParams(input: { cli: readonly ParamArg[]; file?: string; workflowParams: WorkflowParamsSpec }): Promise<Record<string, unknown>>`.
  - `ParamArg = { key: string; rawValue: string }` (parsed by FEAT-012's argv layer; we accept a plain object here so this is unit-testable in isolation).
  - Algorithm:
    1. If `file` provided, read it (`fs/promises.readFile`), parse via the `yaml` package, validate the top level is a plain object (reject arrays, scalars). Errors → `ParamsValidationError` with line/column from the `yaml` parser.
    2. Overlay CLI args on top of file values (CLI wins).
    3. For each entry in `workflowParams` (from the workflow's `params:` block), coerce the value to the declared type: `string` (pass-through), `number` (`Number(v)`, reject NaN), `boolean` (`v === "true"` / `"false"`; reject otherwise), `date` (`new Date(v)` ISO-8601 only). Unrecognized types → `ParamsValidationError`.
    4. Validate required params: any `workflowParams[k].required === true` (default true unless `optional: true` declared) must have a resolved value; otherwise `MissingRequiredParamError` with the full list of missing keys.
    5. Reject params whose **string values** match common credential shapes (the same regex set used by `yantra lint` per memory.md §Security: `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`, `eyJ…`). Params are not secrets; pasting a real password as `--params password=...` is a security mistake, caught at the boundary.
    6. Return the typed record.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (in `params-resolver.spec.ts`):
  - File alone, CLI alone, both — CLI wins on collision.
  - Type coercion: string/number/boolean/date happy paths; `boolean: "yes"` rejected with actionable message; `date: "not a date"` rejected.
  - Missing required param surfaces typed error with **all** missing keys (not just the first).
  - Optional params honored when omitted (no error).
  - Credential-shape rejection: `--params api_key=sk-abc123…` → `ParamsValidationError` with `"params are not secrets — declare a `secrets:` entry instead"`.
  - Malformed YAML in `--params-file` surfaces error with line/column.
  - Empty `cli` and missing `file` returns defaults-only record.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `resolveParams` with `@example`. Add a brief section to `docs/workflow-yaml.md` (owned by FEAT-009; this feature appends only) describing how `--params` and `--params-file` interact.
- **Verify**: `vitest run packages/core/tests/workflow/replay/params-resolver.spec.ts` green on all 3 OS.
- **Depends on**: FEAT-002 (`WorkflowParamsSpec` type), FEAT-009 (workflow YAML schema).

### TASK-002: Workflow → Plan translator

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `workflow-to-plan.ts`.
  - Export `translate(workflow: Workflow, params: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>): TranslatedWorkflow`.
  - Algorithm:
    1. Assign step ids: walk `workflow.steps`, assigning `s1`, `s2`, … in order. If a step already carries an `id` (hand-authored case), keep it; assert uniqueness; reject duplicates with `WorkflowTranslationError`.
    2. For each step, build the Plan step using the FEAT-002 discriminated union. Locator references (the step's `to:` / `from:` fields naming an entry in `_locators`) become `{ kind: "workflow", name }`. `value:` fields naming a secret become `{ kind: "secret", key }`; `value:` fields containing `{{ param:K }}` become `{ kind: "param", key: K }`; `value:` fields containing `{{ capture:K }}` become `{ kind: "capture", key: K }`; literal strings pass through.
    3. Carry `scope` 1:1 onto the Plan step.
    4. Extract `outputBindings` from `workflow.outputs`: parse each `{{ ... }}` JSONata expression; record `retention` from optional `retention:` field (default `"persisted"`).
    5. Compute `profileSpec` from `workflow.cookies`: `"auto"` → `{ kind: "workflow", workflowName: workflow.name }`; `"none"` → `{ kind: "ephemeral" }`. Anything else (forward-compat) currently rejects with `WorkflowTranslationError`.
    6. Collect `declaredSecretKeys` from `workflow.secrets` (used by preflight in TASK-006).
    7. Build the `LocatorTable` directly from `workflow._locators` — no mutation, just typed copy.
    8. Run FEAT-002's `validatePlanSemantics(plan, locatorTable)` as a final check. Any failure → `WorkflowTranslationError` (the workflow was edited between save and run — give a clear path-to-fix).
    9. Return `TranslatedWorkflow`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`workflow-to-plan.spec.ts`):
  - Round-trip fixture workflow (`bank-statement.fixture.yaml`) → Plan; snapshot the Plan; assert all locator references resolved to `workflow`-kind chains.
  - Scope preservation: a step with `scope: read-only-data` produces `plan.steps[i].scope = "read-only-data"`.
  - Step-id assignment is deterministic across runs (snapshot stable).
  - Hand-authored step with duplicate `id` rejected.
  - Unknown cookie mode rejected.
  - Secret reference in a `value:` field that names an undeclared secret → `WorkflowTranslationError` (caught here even if FEAT-002's semantic validator misses it — defense-in-depth).
  - `outputs:` binding whose JSONata is syntactically invalid → `WorkflowTranslationError` at parse time (we parse the expression upfront so eval-time errors are limited to data shape).
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `translate` with `@example` showing the input/output shape. README section "How a Workflow becomes a Plan" referenced by FEAT-009's docs.
- **Verify**: Tests green. Manual: feed `examples/bank-statement.yaml` (shipped with the repo) through `translate` in a Node REPL; output Plan JSON is human-readable.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001 (consumes resolved params for substitution shape), FEAT-002 (Plan + Workflow schemas + semantic validator), FEAT-009 (Workflow shape).

### TASK-003: RunOrchestrator.run() — top-level happy-path

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `run-orchestrator.ts`, `run-store.ts`, `manifest-writer.ts`, `cookies-mode.ts`, `preflight.ts`, `output-evaluator.ts` (skeletons fleshed out by later tasks; this task implements the happy-path glue).
  - `LocalRunStore.createRun(request)`: build `runId` = `<isoCompact>-<workflowName>-<shortUUID>`. `mkdir -p` run dir at mode `0700`. Create `.lock` file with `process.pid` and start timestamp. Return `{ runId, runDir }`.
  - `writeManifest(runDir, manifest)`: atomic write — `<runDir>/manifest.json.tmp` → `fs.rename`. Mode `0600`.
  - `redactParamsForManifest(params, declaredSecretKeys)`: walk param entries; if the *key* is in `declaredSecretKeys` (it shouldn't be — params are never secrets — but defense-in-depth), or the value is a `SecretRef`, replace with `{ kind: "secret", key }`. Pass plain values through.
  - `RunOrchestrator.run(request)`:
    1. Load workflow via `workflowStore.load(request.workflowName)`. If missing → `WorkflowNotFoundError` → `RunOutcome{ kind: "failure" }` with no run dir (validation error before run starts → exit 1 in the CLI).
    2. `resolveParams({ cli, file, workflowParams: workflow.params })` → resolved params.
    3. `translate(workflow, params)` → `TranslatedWorkflow`.
    4. `preflightSecrets(declaredSecretKeys, secretStore)` → fail fast if any missing.
    5. `runStore.createRun(request)` → `{ runId, runDir }`.
    6. Build initial `RunManifest` with `status: "running"`, `startedAt: clock.now()`, redacted params, scopeSummary, llmProvider, cookieMode, profilePath (resolved from `profileSpec` via `browserProvider.profileStore.resolve`). `writeManifest(runDir, manifest)`.
    7. Also write `plan.json` (atomic) — readers (resume, audit) use it.
    8. Construct `ExecutionContext` (FEAT-005 type) with: `runId`, `runDir`, `params`, `locatorTable`, `secretStore`, `sanitizer`, `ethicsGate`, `eventBus` (writes to `events.jsonl`), `budgets`, `browserProvider`, `profileSpec`, `llmClient` (for `llm_summarize` only).
    9. Call `executor.run(plan, ctx)`. Returns `ExecutorOutcome` with `{ status, captures, lastStepId, failureClass? }`.
    10. On `completed`: `evaluateOutputs(outputBindings, { captures, params })` → outputs map. `writeOutputs(runDir, { runId, emittedAt, outputs: filtered-by-retention, retentionPolicy })`. `updateRunStatus(runId, { status: "completed", endedAt })`. Render and write `report.md`. Return `RunOutcome{ kind: "success" }`.
    11. On `failed`: attempt `evaluateOutputs` over whatever captures we have (so partial outputs are still useful); write `outputs.json` (may be empty). `updateRunStatus(runId, { status: "failed", endedAt, failureClass })`. Render and write `report.md`. Return `RunOutcome{ kind: "failure" }`.
    12. On `aborted` (human-handoff or scope-violation): same writes; classify the abort reason from the failure class. Return `RunOutcome{ kind: "aborted" }`.
    13. **`finally` block**: `runStore.releaseLock(runId)`; close any open browser session.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`run-orchestrator.spec.ts`, with fully mocked deps):
  - Happy path: success outcome; `manifest.json` ends with `status: "completed"`; `outputs.json` contains declared outputs; `report.md` exists.
  - Workflow not found → `RunOutcome{ kind: "failure" }`; no run dir created.
  - Missing secret → preflight fires; no browser launch; outcome `failure` with `failureClass: "secret-not-found"`.
  - Executor throws → `report.md` still written; lock released; browser closed (verify via mock `BrowserSession.close()` called).
  - Output evaluation failure → run still completes; `report.md` has a warning section.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `RunOrchestrator.run`, `LocalRunStore`, `writeManifest`. README sketch of the `yantra run` execution lifecycle (mirrors brainstorm §7.3 + §7.6).
- **Verify**: Tests green. Manual: orchestrator run against a stub workflow + stub executor produces a fully populated run dir.
- **Depends on**: TASK-001, TASK-002, FEAT-003 (BrowserProvider + ProfileStore), FEAT-005 (Executor + ExecutionContext + EventBus types), FEAT-006 (SecretStore + Sanitizer + ScopeEnforcer), FEAT-009 (WorkflowStore).

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `report-renderer.ts`.
  - `MarkdownReportRenderer.renderRunReport(report)` builds the markdown string with sections in this order, all populated from `RunReport` (no I/O):

### TASK-006: Preflight — secrets, ethics, workflow lint sanity

### TASK-007: Resume orchestrator — yantra resume <run-id>

> **Plan §4 MVP scope-down**: a checkpoint is a *logical pointer*, NOT a browser-state snapshot. Resume re-launches Chrome, navigates to the last-known URL, re-enters the executor at the next step with captures rehydrated. **If the first replayed step's locator fails to resolve (i.e., the page state has drifted), the run aborts with a clear message advising the user to re-run the workflow from scratch.** MVP does not attempt aggressive state recovery — keeping resume simple is a deliberate scope choice.

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `resume.ts` and add `RunOrchestrator.resume(runId, opts)`.
  - `loadResumePoint(runStore, runId): Promise<ResumePoint>`:
    1. `runStore.getRun(runId)` → if null, `RunDirMissingError`.
    2. Validate `run.status ∈ {"failed", "paused"}`; otherwise `RunNotResumableError` with the current status in the message.
    3. Scan `<runDir>/checkpoints/` for the highest step number; read its JSON (one file per checkpoint; format owned by FEAT-005). Extract `captures`, `params`, and `lastCheckpointStepId`.
    4. Compute `nextStepIndex` = `plan.steps.findIndex(s => s.id === lastCheckpointStepId) + 1`.
    5. Derive `cookieProfilePath` from manifest's `profilePath` (null if ephemeral; for `cookies: none` you cannot resume — surface `RunNotResumableError` with "cookies: none workflows do not preserve state across resumes").
    6. Pull `originalFailureClass` and `originalStartedAt` from manifest.
  - `requiresUserConsent(failureClass): boolean` returns true for `"scope-violation"` and `"ethics-refused"` — these should NOT be retried blindly. The CLI prompts the user; the orchestrator accepts an `opts.confirmRiskyResume?: boolean` and refuses without it.
  - **Stale-resume prompt**: if `now - originalStartedAt > 24h`, the orchestrator accepts an `opts.confirmStaleResume?: boolean` and refuses without it (page state is likely stale; the CLI prompts the user). Plan §4 mandates this.
  - `RunOrchestrator.resume(runId, opts)`:
    1. `loadResumePoint(runStore, runId)` → `ResumePoint`.
    2. If `requiresUserConsent(originalFailureClass)` and not `opts.confirmRiskyResume` → return `RunOutcome{ kind: "aborted", reason: "user-handoff" }` with a clear `report.md` addendum.
    3. If `originalStartedAt` is older than 24h and not `opts.confirmStaleResume` → same abort path with a "stale resume" addendum.
    4. Create a *new* `Run` row (new `runId`, new `taskId`, `parentRunId = original runId`) — append-only. Same workflow, same params (rehydrated from `ResumePoint.params`; secrets re-resolved at execution boundary). Use the **same profileSpec** as the original (same per-workflow profile dir → same cookies).
    5. Build `ExecutionContext` with pre-populated `captures` from the resume point. Emit `task_resumed` event.
    6. Call `executor.run(plan, ctx, { startAt: nextStepIndex })`.
    7. **Drift-abort on first replayed step**: if the first step run after resume produces a `locator_exhausted` failure, the orchestrator catches this *specifically* and aborts the run with `RunOutcome{ kind: "failure", failureClass: "resume-drift" }`. The report.md gets a dedicated section: *"This resume failed at the first step (step `<id>`, locator `<name>`) because the page state has likely changed since the original run on `<startedAt>`. Yantra MVP does not attempt to recover from state drift — please re-run the workflow from scratch (`yantra run <workflow-name>`). If this keeps happening on the same workflow, the site may have changed; re-record the workflow."*
    8. **Drift on later steps**: a `locator_exhausted` failure on a step *after* the first replayed one falls through to the normal failure path (it's likely a real workflow issue, not state drift — the user already proved earlier steps work). Treated as `failureClass: locator_exhausted` per the normal flow.
    9. Proceed identically to `RunOrchestrator.run` from step 10 onward (output eval → outputs.json → manifest update → report.md).
- [ ] **`FailureClass` additions** (coordinate with FEAT-002): `"resume-drift"` joins the enum. Tracked as a discovery item.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`resume.spec.ts`):
  - Resume of a `paused` run at checkpoint step `s4` resumes from step `s5`.
  - Resume of a `completed` run → `RunNotResumableError`.
  - Resume of an `aborted` run with `scope-violation` and no `confirmRiskyResume` → outcome `aborted`; report has a "this run was aborted for a scope violation — resume not allowed without --force" line.
  - Resume of a `failed` run with cookies-none → `RunNotResumableError` with the cookies-none message.
  - Resume creates a new run-dir with `parentRunId` populated; original run dir untouched.
  - `task_resumed` event emitted at start of new run.
  - **First-step locator miss → `resume-drift` failure** with the re-run-from-scratch message in `report.md`.
  - **Stale resume (>24h)** without `confirmStaleResume` → aborted; with it → proceeds normally.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `loadResumePoint`, `requiresUserConsent`, `RunOrchestrator.resume`. Add `docs/run-report-format.md` "Resuming a run" section that explicitly documents the MVP scope-down and the re-run-from-scratch guidance.
- **Verify**: Tests green.
- **Depends on**: TASK-003, TASK-004, FEAT-005 (checkpoint store + `startAt` parameter on `Executor.run`).

### TASK-007a: Chrome version drift advisory + LOCATOR_MISS_IN_UNRECORDED_FRAME diagnostic

> Plan §6 mandates Chrome-drift visibility. Plan §7 mandates the unrecorded-frame diagnostic. Both are diagnostic-only — replay never *fails* on drift, only warns; locator misses inside unrecorded frames produce a clearer error class.

- [ ] **Implementation** — Chrome drift comparison (`replay/chrome-drift.ts`):
  - On `RunOrchestrator.run` start (after browser launch, before plan walk), call `browserProvider.getVersion()` → `{ major, full }` (FEAT-003 surface).
  - Compare against `workflow.recorded_with?.chromeMajor`. If `recorded_with` is null (hand-authored workflow), skip silently.
  - If `|chromeAtRun.major - recordedWith.chromeMajor| > 2`, build `chromeDriftWarning = "recorded under Chrome <X>; running under Chrome <Y> — locator misses may indicate DOM-rendering drift"`. Emit a `chrome_drift_warning` event (kind to be added to FEAT-002 `TaskEvent` union — discovery item) and store the string in `manifest.chromeDriftWarning`.

### TASK-010: Outputs filtering, retention, and on-disk redaction

> Plan §6: `outputs.json` runs through the secret-shape redactor before write (defense-in-depth against credential-shaped strings in authenticated extracts). The pre-redaction values stay in memory for `llm_summarize` consumption; the on-disk artifact is always redacted. A workflow may set `outputs_unredacted: true` to opt out for `read-only-data` scope outputs (FEAT-009 lints the flag).

- [ ] **Implementation**: Flesh out `output-evaluator.ts`.
  - `evaluateOutputs(bindings: OutputBinding[], context: { captures, params, finalCtx }): Promise<EvaluatedOutputs>`:
    - For each binding, evaluate the JSONata expression under the same sandbox config FEAT-005 uses (200 ms timeout, 100 KB result cap, no custom functions). Eval input scope: `{ param: params, capture: captures, previous: finalCtx.previousStep }`. **No `secret_ref` in scope** per plan §7 / FEAT-009 §2.7. Catch eval errors → record as `{ name, error: string }` in result; do NOT throw (per spec — output eval failure is non-fatal).
    - **`ExtractionResultEnvelope` handling** (plan §4 lenient-with-evidence): when a binding references a `capture:<name>` that resolves to an `ExtractionResultEnvelope`, the default projection returns `envelope.rows.filter(r => !('__error' in r))` (valid rows only). The workflow author can opt into the full envelope via JSONata (`{{ capture:transactions }}` returns the envelope object; `{{ capture:transactions.rows }}` returns all rows including errors). Document this in the workflow YAML docs.
    - Filter by `retention`: `outputs.json` receives only `retention: "persisted"` values; transient ones are recorded in the `RunReport` so the renderer can note "transient — not persisted" but are not on disk.
    - **Never** evaluate against unsanitized authenticated content for output binding — the bindings operate on already-extracted `captures`, which are already classified per-step by FEAT-005's scope enforcer. Add an assertion: if a binding tries to project a value classified `authenticated-raw`, log `warn` and emit `null` for that binding (the workflow author should declare a `scope: read-only-data` extract upstream).
  - `EvaluatedOutputs = { persisted: Record<string, unknown>; transient: Record<string, unknown>; errors: readonly { name: string; error: string }[] }`.
- [ ] **`outputs.json` redaction pass** (`output-evaluator.ts → redactOutputsForDisk`):
  - Walk `evaluated.persisted` recursively; for every string value, apply the secret-shape redactor (FEAT-006's `redactSecretShapes` — same regexes as the lint rule `secret-shaped-literal` plus a high-entropy heuristic for ≥24-char strings). Replace matches with `<redacted:secret-shape>`.
  - **Bypass condition**: if `workflow.outputs_unredacted === true` AND the binding's source capture was extracted under `scope: read-only-data`, skip redaction for *that specific output value*. Per plan §6: read-only-data scope is the only place the bypass is legitimate. The bypass decision is recorded in `manifest.scopeSummary` as a `unredactedOutputCount` field for auditability.
  - The pre-redaction `evaluated.persisted` is what `llm_summarize` consumes in-memory during the run; only the disk write goes through the redactor. Tests assert this separation.
- [ ] **Unit Tests** (`output-evaluator.spec.ts`):
  - Simple binding `{{ capture:summary }}` → returns `captures.summary`.
  - JSONata transform `{{ $sum(capture:transactions.amount) }}` → returns numeric sum (per plan §3 example).
  - Binding referencing a missing capture → records error; does not throw; result has `errors: [...]`.
  - Sandbox timeout: a 1s `$sleep`-equivalent (using a recursive expression that fast-check can construct) terminates at 200 ms; error recorded.
  - Result-size cap: a binding that constructs a 1 MB string → error recorded; output not included.
  - Retention filter: `persisted` ends up in `outputs.json` input; `transient` does not.
  - Authenticated-raw projection is refused (returns null + warning).
  - **Extraction envelope default projection** returns only valid rows; full-envelope projection returns rows + metadata.
  - **Secret-shape redaction**: an output containing the literal `"sk-test-FAKEKEY1234567890ABCDEF"` becomes `"<redacted:secret-shape>"` in the on-disk `outputs.json` but is preserved in-memory for `llm_summarize`.
  - **`outputs_unredacted: true` bypass** only applies to outputs sourced from `read-only-data`-scoped extracts; outputs sourced from `authenticated` scope still get redacted regardless of the flag.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: JSDoc on `evaluateOutputs` and `redactOutputsForDisk`. Add an "Outputs, retention, and on-disk redaction" section to workflow YAML docs.
- **Verify**: Tests green.
- **Depends on**: TASK-003, FEAT-005 (JSONata sandbox config + capture classification + `ExtractionResultEnvelope` shape), FEAT-006 (`redactSecretShapes`).

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**:
  - This feature does not handle credentials directly — it delegates entirely to **FEAT-006's `SecretStore`** at the execution boundary (the executor in FEAT-005 calls `secretStore.get(key)` exactly when a `fill` step's `value:` field is a `SecretRef`).
  - **Workflow profile** (FEAT-003) is the only persistence of session state — cookies + localStorage live in the per-workflow Chrome `user-data-dir`. The user is responsible for the initial login (recorded via FEAT-008, or pre-seeded via a manual `record` session). The orchestrator does not attempt to "log in if not logged in" — that's a workflow-author responsibility.
  - `cookies: none` workflows get an ephemeral profile per run; they cannot persist auth state and cannot be resumed (TASK-007 surfaces this).

- **Error Handling**: Per memory.md, every domain failure has a typed custom error class. This feature introduces:
  - `WorkflowNotFoundError` — `workflowStore.load(name)` returned null. Carries `{ workflowName, workflowsDir }`.
  - `ParamsValidationError` — bad `--params-file` YAML; type-coercion failure; secret-shaped value in a param. Carries `{ paramName, reason, value? (sanitized) }`.
  - `MissingRequiredParamError` — declared required params absent. Carries `{ missing: readonly string[] }`.
  - `WorkflowTranslationError` — Workflow → Plan translation drift (duplicate step ids, undeclared secret reference, bad JSONata in outputs, unknown cookie mode). Carries `{ workflowPath, offendingPath, reason }`.
  - `RunNotResumableError` — resume target is in a non-resumable state. Carries `{ runId, currentStatus, reason }`.
  - `RunDirMissingError` — `getRun(runId)` returned null. Carries `{ runId, expectedPath }`.
  - `RunDirLockedError` — `.lock` file present and PID alive (best-effort). Carries `{ runId, holdingPid }`.
  - `OutputEvaluationError` — JSONata eval failed for a binding. **Non-fatal** — recorded in `RunReport`, run still terminates normally. Carries `{ bindingName, reason }`.
  - **Every run-aborting failure produces a `report.md`.** The orchestrator's `run()` body is wrapped in a `try/catch/finally` whose `catch` writes a minimal report even if the failure is in the orchestrator itself (e.g., disk-full). Property test in TASK-003 / TASK-011 verifies.
  - **Bounded retries are FEAT-005's responsibility**, not this feature's. The orchestrator surfaces the outcome; the executor decides what to retry.
  - Resume gating: `requiresUserConsent(failureClass)` returns true for `scope-violation` and `ethics-refused` per memory.md §Security (these should NOT be retried blindly).

- **Logging**: Pino, per memory.md. Per-run log child created at `RunOrchestrator.run` start with `{runId, workflowName}` bindings — every log line carries those automatically. Levels:
  - `info` — `"run started"` (runId, workflow, params count); `"run completed"` (runId, status, durationMs); `"resume started"` (runId, parentRunId, fromStepId).
  - `warn` — `"workflow translation warning"` (FEAT-009 lint warnings surfaced at translate time); `"output evaluation failed"` (binding name + reason); `"run dir lock stale"` (PID dead but lock present — proceed).
  - `error` — `"run aborted"` paired with `task_failed` event; `"manifest write failed"` (disk full — falls through to a degraded report).
  - `debug` — Workflow→Plan diff; param-coercion details; preflight check results.
  - **Never log**: the `params` map verbatim (it may contain PII even if not secret); the resolved profile path (FEAT-003 already redacts); literal capture values (PII risk — log capture *keys* only).
  - **Events emitted** (consumed by `events.jsonl` via FEAT-005's bus; this feature is a producer for some): `task_started` (at run start), `task_resumed` (new — added to FEAT-002's `TaskEvent` union if not present; discovery item below), `task_completed`, `task_failed`. Step-level events come from FEAT-005.

- **Security**:
  - **Manifest never contains secret values.** `redactParamsForManifest` walks every param value; any `SecretRef` shape becomes `{ kind:"secret", key }`. A property test in TASK-005 generates random param maps with embedded `SecretRef`s and asserts the rendered `manifest.json` contains no literal secret value.
  - **`report.md` never contains secret values.** The renderer reads `events.jsonl` which is already sanitized by FEAT-005's emitter. Property test in TASK-005's no-leak section confirms.
  - **`outputs.json` never contains secret values.** Output bindings operate on `captures`, which are already classified by FEAT-005's scope enforcer; the evaluator (TASK-010) additionally refuses to project from `authenticated-raw` captures.
  - **Secrets resolve only at execution boundary** (FEAT-006 contract). This orchestrator never calls `secretStore.get(key)` — preflight uses `has` only.
  - **Params are not secrets.** TASK-001 rejects credential-shaped values in `--params` with an actionable error pointing the user at the `secrets:` block.
  - **Run-dir lockfile** prevents accidental concurrent resume; defense-in-depth against double-running a paused run from two terminals.
  - **Scope-violation runs are not blindly resumable** (TASK-007's `requiresUserConsent` gate). Memory.md §Security: "the `read-only-data` scope statically rejects mutating step verbs — the executor enforces this before any browser instantiation" — this feature honors that by refusing to re-run a scope-violated workflow without explicit user consent.
  - **Ethics-refused runs are not blindly resumable** — same gate. A workflow that hit a blocklist or robots.txt deny should not be re-run by `yantra resume` without the user re-examining the workflow.

- **Testing**:
  - All unit tests tagged `@no-llm` (per memory.md: replay is deterministic; this feature is on the spine — mandatorily LLM-free).
  - Property tests: TASK-003 (orchestrator robustness — always returns RunOutcome, never throws), TASK-005 (no-leak property on the renderer), TASK-010 (sandbox timeout + size-cap).
  - E2E test (TASK-011) is the dogfooding acceptance gate. Memory.md §Testing names it explicitly as the recorder/replay round-trip suite.
  - Cross-OS matrix: every spec runs on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest` from day one (per memory.md). The e2e test in TASK-011 specifically exercises path handling on each OS.
  - Tests **never** spawn real Chrome in unit specs — that's e2e only. Unit specs mock `BrowserProvider.launch` to return a stub session.
  - Snapshot tests (TASK-005's report renderer) use a stable clock and stable run-id so the snapshots don't churn on every run.

## Notes for the Implementer (non-normative)

- The Workflow → Plan translation is the *conceptual heart* of this feature. Resist the urge to define a separate "executable Plan" shape — the goal is for the agent (FEAT-011) and the workflow loader (this feature) to produce **the same `Plan` shape**, so the executor has one execution path. The only difference is the `LocatorTable` — agent-produced Plans get an empty one (and use a different `LocatorChain.kind` for direct selectors); workflow-produced Plans attach the workflow's `_locators`.
- The orchestrator deliberately does **not** own retries, ethics checks, or scope enforcement — those live in FEAT-005's executor. This feature's job is *lifecycle management*: load → translate → preflight → run → report. Keep the orchestrator thin; resist scope creep.
- The atomic-write convention (`tmp` + `rename`) for manifest.json and outputs.json is non-negotiable. A crash mid-write should leave the previous version intact, not a half-written file. Test it explicitly (TASK-004).
- Resume of a `cookies: none` workflow is fundamentally not safe — the session state is gone. The orchestrator refuses; do not try to "rerun from step 0" as a fallback, that defeats the user's expectation that `resume` means continue.
- The e2e test (TASK-011) uses a hand-authored workflow YAML rather than recording in CI because recording involves visible Chrome + user-event timing, which is flaky in CI. FEAT-008's e2e tests cover the recording side; this feature's e2e covers the replay side. Together they make the full round-trip — separately runnable, both gating.
- The `parentRunId` chain for resumes can grow long if a user repeatedly resumes a failing workflow. We don't compact it in MVP — disk is cheap and the audit trail of "what was tried" is valuable.
